title: Selective costly behavioral response to an acknowledged-reason challenge
target_claim: Among adults who endorse a specified compensatory reason, an explicit scope challenge increases delayed costly transfer to unfamiliar matched recipients and changes transfer more in matched than disanalogy cases, beyond equally informative factual exposure and recipient perspective exercises, without a practically important increase in explicit misapplication of that reason.
not_tested: Derivation of the first positive normative commitment
All-things-considered moral correctness of a particular transfer
Actual population prevalence outside the enrolled panel
The pooled effect identifies removal of a previously held scope restriction or newly learned internal concern

population.sampling_frame: One named online panel, country and language frozen before recruitment
population.eligibility: Consenting adults who comprehend and endorse the specified compensatory reason at screening at least seven days before assignment
population.n_status: Design choice pending blinded power and attrition assessment before external registration

allocation.seed_status: Must be generated by an independent custodian and frozen before recruitment
allocation.shared_material: Identical verified recipient facts and testimony; matched time, reading burden, credibility, and payment
allocation.unavoidable_contrast: Instructional framing differs and is part of the treatment

stake.recipient: Separately consenting actual participant with verified workload, compensation record, and preference
stake.decision: Allocate optional endowed bonus; one decision randomly selected for actual payment under a disclosed rule

primary_outcomes.matched_transfer: Participant mean fraction of decision budget transferred on new matched cases, bounded in [0,1]
primary_outcomes.disanalogy_misapplication: Participant mean rate of explicitly applying the specified compensatory reason where its supplied grounds do not hold, bounded in [0,1]; additional generosity for another reason is not automatically an error
primary_outcomes.behavioral_selectivity: Participant matched-case transfer mean minus disanalogy-case transfer mean, bounded in [-1,1]; this tests differential behavior, not the moral wrongness of generosity or the private motive for a transfer

analysis.estimand: Stratification-adjusted intention-to-treat differences in participant-level means in the randomized panel cohort
analysis.interval_method: Freeze an asymptotically justified robust or studentized randomization interval implementation before registration; validate by blinded simulation. No sharp-null test may be represented as general weak-null inference.
analysis.missingness: Retain randomized denominators. For transfer lower bounds assign missing reason-arm outcomes 0 and missing control outcomes 1; reverse for upper bounds. For error upper bounds assign missing reason-arm outcomes 1 and missing control outcomes 0; reverse for lower bounds. For behavioral-selectivity lower bounds assign missing reason-arm selectivity -1 and missing control selectivity +1; reverse for upper bounds. Bound partially missing matched and disanalogy case means separately before subtraction. Recompute the correspondingly allocated confidence bounds. Practical support requires all six margins under adverse assignments. Otherwise practical settlement is inconclusive even if completion-only analysis passes.
analysis.multiplicity: Six simultaneous two-sided intervals, Bonferroni family alpha 0.05; favorable and opposite bounds use this same family. Missing-data envelopes use the correspondingly allocated one-sided bounds, with the full coverage argument frozen before registration.

decision.scoped_practical_support: Both transfer lower simultaneous bounds exceed 0.10, both behavioral-selectivity lower bounds exceed 0.05, and both error upper bounds are below 0.05, under adverse missingness assignments and with integrity checks satisfied
decision.positive_only_evidence: Report each positive transfer or selectivity lower bound exceeding 0 separately; failure to exceed its practical margin does not settle that margin, and increased matched transfer with unchanged stated discrimination alone does not identify selective behavioral transfer
decision.practical_rejection: Using the same simultaneous interval family, an upper bound on transfer advantage is below 0.10 or an upper bound on selectivity advantage is below 0.05; report each comparison separately
decision.adverse: Using the same simultaneous interval family, a lower bound on excess reason misapplication exceeds 0.05, or an upper bound on matched-transfer difference is below 0
decision.otherwise: Inconclusive or mixed; do not collapse into success
decision.margins_are: Prospective design assumptions to be debated before outcomes, not findings

stop_rules.fixed_stop: Registered sample size or registered calendar cutoff, whichever comes first

required_before_launch: Name population, panel, recruitment dates, payments, and funder
Finalize recipient consent and independent verification of work and prior compensation
Finalize scripts and reason applicability coding with independent reviewers
Conduct blind feasibility and power study without choosing outcomes from main data
Freeze sample, calendar cutoff, allocation code, analysis implementation, margins, and the specified adverse missingness rule
Secure applicable human-participant review and privacy arrangements
Externally register and timestamp the final protocol
revision_record: Version 2 adds behavioral selectivity so uniformly increased giving alone cannot pass, and allocates simultaneous coverage to both directions used for support and rejection. No data were collected.
Pooled target narrowed to selective behavioral response because eligibility includes already-inclusive participants; no pooled scope-removal inference.

secondary_outcomes.baseline_restriction: Report baseline restrictions and changes in stated reason admission; subgroup analyses remain exploratory under this draft
secondary_outcomes.construct_limit: Eligibility includes already-inclusive participants. A pooled pass can demonstrate selective behavioral response without showing removal of a prior exclusion. A confirmatory scope-revision claim needs a prespecified restriction/removal estimand with adequate recruitment, power and error allocation.
